clusters.text: New Delhi The Supreme Court has cleared the decks for the income-tax assessments of the two businessmen sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal over share transactions that funded their purchase of a prime property on Delhi's Sikandra Road in 2010. A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, while upholding income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10. Justice Sabharwal served as the 36th Chief Justice of India (November 1, 2005 to January 14, 2007) and had a long judicial career spanning the Delhi High Court, Bombay High Court, and the Supreme Court of India. The top court said the notice issued by the Income Tax Department dated March 31, 2015, rested on valid "reason to believe" under Sections 147 and 148 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. The apex court, in its October 28 judgment, said the probe report by the director general provided tangible material for the Assessing Officer to form a reasonable belief that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment. It said "reason to believe" means cause or justification, and the officer need not have finally proved the escape of income. It said Courts cannot weigh the sufficiency of the reasons and rejected the argument that overvaluation cannot lead to escaped income. "The escapement of income at the hands of the seller of the shares, the proceeds of which were later utilised to acquire capital assets to thus claim deduction, could as well be a diversion of income, assessable to tax under the guise of sale proceeds which, in the present case, assumes relevance for reason of the sale proceeds being far above the actual value of the shares.... "The present case is not one wherein it could be said that the Assessing Officer had only a vague feeling on the basis of which he recorded that proper investigation was necessary. We are of the view that a conclusion that the truth of the alleged transactions needs to be investigated is not the same thing as having reasons, post investigation, to issue a notice," the bench said. In October 2007, the Sabharwal brothers and two other shareholders agreed to sell shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and SVIIT Software (P) Ltd to GYS Real Estate Pvt Ltd. clusters.text: Oppo flagships were never cheap, but the latest generation may be too expensive to achieve the popularity that it deserves, given the excellent hardware of the phones themselves. The Oppo Find X models aren’t alone in this – memory prices rising hundreds of percent in a matter of months made this outcome inevitable. The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max is the clear winner of the two – this is how it goes usually when comparing very expensive flagships. People who think they are too expensive already voted “no, thanks”, which leaves the money-is-no-object crowd that just wants the best. The Find X10 Pro Max just may prove to be the best flagship of 2026. If Oppo had called it an “Ultra”, we wouldn’t have argued much against that. But there is an Ultra coming and around 10% of voters want to wait for it. Twice as many voters are looking at flagships from other brands. The Pro Max certainly has its fans, but judging by the poll results, only around a quarter of those fans are actually willing to buy a unit at its launch price. More may join in if and when Oppo is able to cut the price. The Oppo Find X10 didn’t do so well – it’s cheaper but not cheap enough to win many people over. This poll shows stronger interest in other flagships than the other poll, both towards the Pro Max and towards flagships from other brands. Around one in five fans are willing to pay the current price of the X10 – as we noted in last week’s poll , you might be able to find a Find X9 Ultra for the same price or get close to it. This undercuts the vanilla X10 as it doesn’t have the latest hardware (e.g. the Dimensity 9600M is really a 9500-class chip), so the X9 Ultra doesn’t feel as old by comparison (it has a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset). We’d love to tell you that discounts are coming, but SK hynix, the third largest DRAM maker in the world, warned that memory shortages will last through 2030. So, there will be some discounts eventually, but they may be smaller than what we are used to. clusters.text: New Delhi The Centre has scrapped the special additional excise duty (SAED) on petrol exports while raising the levy on high-speed diesel to Rs 11.5 per litre and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) to Rs 11 per litre, according to notifications issued by the Ministry of Finance. Petrol export duty scrapped; diesel and ATF levies raised Under the new notification, the SAED on petrol exports has been reduced to nil from Rs 2.5 per litre, while the levy on high-speed diesel exports has been increased to Rs 11.5 per litre from Rs 8.5 per litre. Export levies introduced amid West Asia crisis The Centre introduced export levies on petrol, diesel and ATF from March 27, 2026, amid the West Asia crisis, with the stated objective of ensuring domestic availability of petroleum products by discouraging exports. The duties were introduced as international energy prices and supply uncertainties raised concerns over the availability of petroleum products in the domestic market. The government has been reviewing the applicable rates every fortnight, taking into account average international prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF during the period since the previous review. Fortnightly reviews lead to repeated revisions The rates have consequently undergone several revisions since their introduction, reflecting movements in international prices. The previous revision, effective October 16, had fixed the SAED on petrol exports at Rs 2.5 per litre, diesel at Rs 8.5 per litre and ATF at Rs 10.5 per litre. The latest changes, therefore, remove the levy on petrol exports while increasing the duties applicable to diesel and ATF exports. It noted that Supreme Court had disapproved of a similar approach in its Aug 5, 2026 order in the Sunil Kumar Singh appeal.According to the court, excluding the defective questions ensures equal treatment for all candidates, as it neither rewards nor penalises anyone for their choice on a question that lacked a single correct answer.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news. clusters.text: A Lufthansa crew member and another foreign national have died following an incident at the swimming pool of Conrad Bengaluru on October 30, 2026. Initial reports suggest that the two men may have suffered electric shocks while using the pool. Two other people, including a hotel employee who attempted to rescue them, were also injured. The deceased have been identified as Alexander Maximilian Theiss, a 57-year-old German national and Lufthansa crew member, and Juraj Horvat, a 45-year-old Slovakian national employed as a project manager with IBM. The incident took place at the swimming pool on the third floor of Conrad Bengaluru, in the Ulsoor neighbourhood. According to reports, the two men were using the pool when they were apparently electrocuted. The exact circumstances surrounding the incident are still being investigated. Two other people were injured while attempting to rescue the victims. They have been identified as Mathew Desantis, a 41-year-old American national staying at the hotel, and Rahul Tiwari, a 28-year-old Indian national working as a pool attendant. Both were taken to Manipal Hospital for treatment and were reported to be out of danger. Lufthansa has confirmed that one of its crew members died in an accident during a layover in Bengaluru. The airline expressed its condolences to the family, friends and colleagues of the deceased. The German publication BILD has reported that the incident may have been linked to the swimming pool’s underwater lighting system. However, this has not been independently established, and the precise source of the suspected electrical fault remains unclear. Bengaluru Police have registered a case and are investigating the incident. The investigation will need to establish how the electrical fault occurred and whether there were any lapses in the installation, inspection or maintenance of the pool’s electrical systems. clusters.title: 6 sites approved in Ranchi for sale of Diwali firecrackers
also: Ranchi Firecracker Sale Sites: Six Locations Approved
clusters.text: Ranchi: The district administration has approved five locations in the city as designated cluster sites for sale of Diwali fireworks this year. Temporary retail stalls at the cluster sites will operate from Nov 4 to 8, officials said.Five retail locations include Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, Bariatu Housing Ground, Shastri Ground in Chutia, Seth Sitaram Ground in Doranda, and the site opposite Harmu Kali Ground. Temporary wholesale outlets will be set up at Morabadi Ground to serve bulk buyers and small vendors.Yogesh Kumar of Trade Friends, a local wholesale fireworks firm, said, “Small vendors from Ranchi and nearby places also come here to buy fireworks for setting up their businesses before Diwali. If the wholesale shops are too far for them to reach, they can come to Morabadi Ground and buy products.”Shayan Zafar, president of the Chotanagpur Fireworks Dealers Association (CFDA), welcomed the cluster model, saying centralised sale points help manage festive crowds and reduce safety risks.“Every year, around 1,200 vendors are provided license to set up temporary shops at the designated places. The move is to ensure that firecrackers are being sold legally, and safely,” he said.Under licensing rules, traders can sell only certified green crackers. Licence holders must obtain a no objection certificate from the fire service department and follow safety directives, including keeping buckets of sand and water, fire extinguishers, and heavy blankets at every stall. Testing or bursting fireworks within 50 metres of the stalls is prohibited.“As wholesale dealers, we do not supply products to any trader who lacks a valid license from the district administration, as doing so would invite strict action against both the wholeseller and the retail vendor. We also educate traders on mandatory safety standards and regulatory guidelines,” Zafar added.The setup saw brief friction on Friday night when Ranchi Municipal Corporation issued notices barring stalls outside Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, calling it its property and warning of legal action. On Saturday, DC Manjunath Bhajantri said it was a misunderstanding and the issue had been resolved.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

clusters.title: Prayagraj weather update: Morning mist likely on November 1, check IMD's temperature forecast
clusters.text: Prayagraj is likely to experience fog or mist during the early morning hours on Sunday, November 1, as weather conditions gradually improve following rainfall over the past few days. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast a minimum temperature of 19 degrees Celsius and a maximum of 27 degrees Celsius for the city, with mainly clear skies expected over the coming days.According to the IMD's local weather forecast, fog or mist is likely during the early morning hours on November 1. The minimum temperature is expected to fall to 19 degrees Celsius, while the maximum could reach 27 degrees Celsius during the day. The weather office has forecast mainly clear skies from November 2 onwards.Prayagraj weather: Rainfall recorded in the past 24 hoursThe recent spell of rain has brought changes in temperature and increased moisture levels across Prayagraj. According to the IMD's weather report dated October 31, the city recorded 5.5 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 am that day.The maximum temperature on October 31 stood at 26.2 degrees Celsius, while the minimum was recorded at 21.2 degrees Celsius, which was 3.2 degrees above normal. Relative humidity was high, reaching 96% at 8:30 am and 90% at 5:30 pm.The increased moisture in the atmosphere is consistent with the forecast of fog or mist during the early hours of November 1.Prayagraj weather forecast for the coming daysThe IMD has indicated a gradual improvement in weather conditions, with mainly clear skies expected from November 2. The maximum temperature is forecast to reach 28 degrees Celsius on November 2 and 3, before rising to 29 degrees Celsius on November 4.The minimum temperature is expected to remain between 18 and 19 degrees Celsius during this period.
